title: Primary and secondary prevention
missing: ASCVD status, risk category from official calculator, CAC if used, Lp(a), family history
evaluate: Establish ASCVD yes/no first; primary prevention uses the pathway's risk tool; secondary prevention skips calculators
consider: High-intensity statin first; add ezetimibe then PCSK9 therapy to reach goal (textbook p.372-373; ACC/AHA 2026; ESC/EAS 2025)
refer: Persistent LDL-C above goal on combination therapy; LDL-C >=190

title: ACS / post-ACS
missing: Date of ACS, current LDL-C, prior statin
consider: Start/intensify statin immediately; early combination (ezetimibe, PCSK9) when far from goal — ESC 2025 and LAI favour early target attainment (LAI: ideally within 2 weeks); recent ACS is a major-event definition (textbook p.361)

title: Diabetes
missing: Duration, target-organ damage, ASCVD status, HbA1c
evaluate: Secondary causes of TG; apoB in diabetes at goal (ACC/AHA 2026)
consider: Diabetes is a high-risk condition; statin per risk category; TG control via glycaemia, weight

title: CKD and dialysis
missing: eGFR, albuminuria, dialysis status, nephrotic features
consider: CKD eGFR 15-59 is a high-risk condition (textbook). Renal dosing of rosuvastatin and fibrates; dialysis initiation evidence not in textbook — nephrology input (unverified)

title: FH and cascade screening
missing: Untreated LDL-C, family history details, xanthomas/arcus, DNA
evaluate: DLCN score tab; exclude secondary causes; Lp(a)
consider: Statin plus ezetimibe, PCSK9 mAb; cascade screening of first-degree relatives; consider genetic testing
refer: Suspected HoFH (LDL-C very high, xanthomas in childhood); children

title: Severe hypertriglyceridaemia
missing: TG on repeat, alcohol, diabetes control, drugs, pregnancy, pancreatitis history
evaluate: Repeat fasting TG; glucose/HbA1c, TSH, creatinine, liver tests
consider: Remove secondary causes, very low fat diet, fibrate; avoid bile-acid sequestrants; textbook: FCS needs <15% fat diet

title: Elevated Lp(a)
evaluate: Measure once; keep units as reported
consider: Optimise LDL-C and other risk factors; PCSK9 mAbs lower Lp(a) modestly (off-label for this); apheresis for extreme cases; Lp(a)-specific drugs investigational
refer: Very high Lp(a) with progressive disease despite control

title: Statin-associated symptoms / suspected intolerance
missing: Symptoms, timing, CK, drug interactions, hypothyroidism, vitamin D, doses tried
evaluate: Exclude hypothyroidism, interacting drugs; dechallenge-rechallenge (textbook p.372)
consider: Switch statin, lower dose/alternate-day, then ezetimibe, bempedoic acid, PCSK9 therapy

title: Older adults and frailty
evaluate: Age >=65 is a high-risk condition (2018-era textbook); shared decision
consider: Evidence-based statin in secondary prevention; individualise intensity (guideline detail not in textbook)

title: Women, pregnancy planning, pregnancy, breastfeeding
evaluate: Confirm pregnancy status before drug start; third-trimester TG rise (textbook p.394)
consider: Statins generally stopped in pregnancy; ACC/AHA 2026 continues to advise discontinuation except rare very-high-risk cases; no approved TG drug in pregnancy per textbook; check current drug labels

title: Children and adolescents
evaluate: FH criteria in children (LDL-C >95th percentile); cascade
consider: Lifestyle cornerstone; statin timing evolving; evolocumab effective in adolescents (textbook p.375)

title: Liver disease, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, other secondary causes
missing: TSH, LFTs, urine albumin, alcohol, drugs
consider: Treat the underlying cause before escalating lipid drugs; resolution often partial (textbook p.364)

title: Drug-induced dyslipidaemia and interactions
evaluate: Review Table 10-5 agents (cyclosporine, amiodarone, thiazides, steroids, oestrogens, retinoids, protease inhibitors, antipsychotics, etc.)
consider: Stop or substitute offending drug when possible; statin interactions (CYP3A4 inhibitors, cyclosporine) — verify against label
